About Me

I am a highly motivated and research-oriented M.Phil Physics graduate with a strong academic background in materials science and nanotechnology. My research interests focus on spinel ferrites, magnetic nanomaterials, and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-based composites. I am enthusiastic about exploring advanced materials, their physical properties, and potential technological applications. I aspire to pursue a PhD in Physics to strengthen my research capabilities, contribute to innovative scientific advancements, and develop a successful career in academic research.

Thesis Title

THE STRUCTURAL, DIELECTRIC AND MAGNETIC PROPERTIES OF MWCNT INTEGRATED Mn0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4 SPINEL FERRITE COMPOSITES SYNTHESIZED BY SOL-GEL AUTO COMBUSTION METHOD.

The research investigated Mn0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4 ferrite composites incorporating multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs), with attention to structural, dielectric/electrical and magnetic characteristics.

Research Objectives

  • To synthesize single-phase Mn-Zn spinel ferrite by sol-gel auto-combustion
  • To prepare MWCNT/ferrite composites with different MWCNT weight percentages (0 to ~5 wt%)
  • To confirm spinel phase formation and study structural changes (XRD, FTIR, Raman, SEM)
  • To analyze dielectric and electrical behavior (LCR meter, I-V)
  • To study magnetic behavior (VSM) and tune properties for electronic and magnetic devices

Research Methodology and Characterization

  • Synthesis and processing: sol-gel auto-combustion method and preparation of ferrite/MWCNT composites.
  • Structural characterization: X-ray Diffraction (XRD), including phase identification and crystallite/lattice analysis.
  • Spectroscopic and morphological characterization: FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, UV-Visible spectroscopy, and SEM/TEM techniques.
  • Dielectric/electrical measurements: LCR measurements, dielectric parameters, AC conductivity and impedance analysis.
  • Magnetic characterization: Vibrating Sample Magnetometer (VSM) measurements for magnetic parameters.
  • Data work: graph plotting, interpretation, and scientific reporting using Origin, MATLAB and Excel.

Research and Technical Skills

  • Materials research: ferrite nanoparticles and ferrite/MWCNT composites.
  • Characterization techniques listed in CV: XRD, FTIR, SEM/TEM, UV-Visible spectroscopy, Raman spectroscopy, LCR and VSM.
  • Data and computing: Origin, MATLAB, Excel, Python, C++, and intermediate knowledge of C, C++ and MATLAB.
  • Instrumentation: oscilloscope, multimetre, and LCR meter.
  • Research practice: literature review, data interpretation, scientific report/thesis writing, research presentations, and laboratory safety.

Research Experience

Laboratory and Experimental Research Experience: Conducted experimental research on Mn0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4/MWCNT composites prepared using the sol-gel auto-combustion method. Proposed PhD Research Interests

My intended doctoral research direction is closely aligned with my M.Phil. research on MWCNT-integrated Mn0.5Zn0.5Fe2O4 spinel ferrite composites synthesized using the sol-gel auto-combustion method. My proposed research may focus on the development and characterization of ferrite-based nanocomposites and other functional nanomaterials, with particular emphasis on understanding how composition, microstructure, and interfacial interactions influence their dielectric, electrical, and magnetic properties. I am also interested in exploring their potential applications in electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding, microwave absorption, and other functional material technologies. The final research topic will be refined according to the expertise of the prospective supervisor, the research priorities of the selected Russian university, and its official doctoral research requirements.

Academic Strengths

Analytical and quantitative problem-solving; experimental design and measurement; data analysis and graphical presentation; scientific writing and presentations; independent work and teamwork; communication, organisation, planning and time management.
